data.narrative:
Deep Fission, a nuclear energy company founded by Liz and Rich Muller, is approaching IPO stage after raising $80M in total capital. The valuation universe consists of 9 comparable companies: 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 6 private-stage peers including Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy, all operating in the frontier nuclear sector.

The peer-median method proved inapplicable to this analysis. Despite identifying 6 same-sector peers in nuclear energy, the narrow-stage and valuation-tier filters yielded insufficient datapoints for reliable comparison—zero matches at the same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier were available. The minimum threshold of three comparable observations could not be met, making a narrow peer median unreliable. An all-sector median approach was rejected as misleading given Deep Fission's specialized position.

No triangulated valuation range can be supported by the available data. The analysis cannot proceed without either (1) expanding the peer set to include adjacent-stage or broader-tier nuclear companies, with explicit notation of methodology shifts, or (2) applying alternative methods such as discounted cash flow analysis or comparable transaction multiples. The primary valuation uncertainty stems from the thinness of IPO-stage comparables in frontier nuclear technology, a characteristic that will require methodological flexibility and heightened disclosure around peer selection rationale.
